question: On which of these small savings product can an investor have a tax benefit on the interest income earned?
explanation:
Investments made in the NSC VIII issue enjoy tax benefits under section 80C of Income Tax Act, 1961. Accrued interest is taxable, but is it deemed to be reinvested and therefore the interest becomes eligible for Section 80C benefits

	In Kisan Vikas Patra - There is no tax incentive for the investment made and the interest earned is taxed on accrual basis.

	In Post Office Time Deposit - The interest earned on these investments is added to the depositor’s total annual income in the year of receipt and is liable to be taxed as per the tax rate of the investor.

question: A person is investing in shares whose market prices are lower than their book value. This style of investing is generally known as ______ .
explanation:
Value investing is an investment strategy that involves picking stocks that appear to be trading for less than their intrinsic or book value. 

	It is an investment strategy that involves purchasing stocks or securities that are under-priced.

question: Bond A carries an interest rate of 9%. Interest rates in the economy for such similar bonds increase to 9.5%. Other things remaining the same. the price of Bond A in secondary market will ______ .
explanation: The price of the bonds in the secondary market will respond to changes in interest rates. An increase in interest rates sees the price of existing bonds depreciate and vice versa.

question: In the New Fund Offer (NFO) of a Mutual Fund, the units are offered at ______ .
explanation: Allotment of units in a Mutual Fund NFO are at the issue price which is typically at the face value of the units.

question: Which of these compliant(s) cannot be addressed on SCORES?
options: Complaints in respect of unlisted companies
Complaints in respect of insurance products or companies
explanation:
SCORES is the online investor redressal mechanism set up by SEBI to deal with the complaints of investors related to all products and entities regulate by it. 

	It does not deal with the following complaints:

	• Complaints against unlisted/delisted/wound up/liquidated/sick companies 

	• Complaints that are sub-judice (relating to cases which are under consideration by court of law, quasi-judicial proceedings etc.) 

	• Complaints falling under the purview of other regulatory bodies

	Insurance sector is not regulated by SEBI. It’s regulated by Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

question: Mr. Sumeet invested Rs 5000 in a Mutual Fund on 1 Jan 2020 and when he redeemed on 31 Dec 2021 he got Rs 12000. Calculate the CAGR.
explanation:
The number of years from 1 Jan 20 to 31 Dec 2021 = 2 years

	Formula for calculating Compounded Annual Growth Rate :

	CAGR = { Ending Value / Begining Value } ^  ( 1 / No. of years)    -   1.

	            =  { 12000 / 5000 } ^ 1 / 2      -  1

	            =  {2.4}  ^ 0.5   -  1

	On the scientific calculator of your computer type 2.4 then press x^y the .5

	          =  1.549 - 1

	          = .549 x 100  =  54.90%

question: To have better clarity in the Investment Policy Document, the goals of the investor should be categorised on the basis of ______ .
explanation: The Investment policy document would normally list out the goals of the investor along with their priorities. This is followed by listing out the investment objectives along with the time horizon. Clarity on this front is essential because the portfolio manager can then frame strategies accordingly.

question: Which of these is TRUE with respect to liquidity in a solution-oriented mutual fund scheme?
options: Solution-oriented mutual fund schemes are close-end funds and can be traded on a stock exchange
Solution-oriented mutual fund schemes are open-end funds and can be easily sold and purchased
Solution-oriented mutual fund schemes can only be purchased during a NFO and are locked in for the entire term
Solution-oriented mutual fund schemes have a lock-in of 5 years
explanation:
SEBI has categorised the open-end solution oriented schemes as follows:

	- Retirement Fund are schemes oriented towards saving for retirement. Schemes will have a lock-in for at least 5 years or till retirement age whichever is earlier.

	- Children’s Fund are schemes oriented towards saving for children’s needs. Schemes will have a lock-in of 5 years or till the age of majority whichever is earlier

question: Identify the securities which can be dematerialized as per Indian regulations?
explanation:
Under the SEBI (Depository and Participants) Regulations of 1996, the categories of securities eligible for dematerialisation are:

	1. Shares, scrips, stocks, bonds, debentures, debenture stock or other marketable security of any incorporated company or other body corporate.

	2. Units of a mutual fund, rights under a collective investment scheme, venture capital funds, certificates of deposit, commercial paper, money market instruments, government securities and unlisted securities.

question: Identify which of these is a part of the Code of Conduct prescribed for intermediaries under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations?
options: During the conduct of the business, the intermediary will be responsible for acts of commission and omission of its employees
The fees charged by an intermediary for the services which he has rendered will be in line with other intermediaries offering similar service
Permission has to be taken from the client by the intermediary before disclosing information of the client in compliance with any law
explanation:
As per the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 Code of Conduct and Ethics :

	High Standards of Service -

	An intermediary shall ensure that it and its key management personnel, employees, contractors and agents, shall in the conduct of their business, observe high standards of integrity, dignity, fairness, ethics and professionalism and all Professional dealings shall be affected in a prompt, effective and efficient manner. An intermediary shall be responsible for the acts or omissions of its employees and agents in respect to the conduct of its business.

question: The Modern Portfolio Theory uses Expected Returns, Standard deviation of asset classes and __________ to create an optimal portfolio.
options: Correlation Coefficient of the Asset classes
explanation:
Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) — developed by Harry Markowitz — is used to construct an optimal portfolio by balancing risk and return. It uses the following key inputs:

	- Expected Returns of each asset

	- Standard Deviation (i.e., risk/volatility) of each asset

	- Correlation Coefficient (or Covariance) between asset classes. This measures how the assets move in relation to each other. Diversification benefit comes from combining assets that are not perfectly correlated.

	(Expected market performance is Not a direct input in MPT and  Portfolio variance is an output, not an input)

question: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to lock-in period in children’s funds.
options: Units in a children’s fund are locked in for 5 years or till the end of tenor of scheme, whichever is earlier
Units in a children’s fund are locked in for 5 years or till age of majority, whichever is earlier
Units in a children’s fund are locked in for a minimum of 5 years and a maximum of 10 years
Units in a children’s fund are locked in for 5 years before child’s majority
explanation: Children’s Fund are schemes oriented towards saving for children’s needs. Schemes will have a lock-in of 5 years or till the age of majority whichever is earlier.

question: For which category of goals can an investor consider a high yield credit risk fund?
options: Near term goals which have a high priority
Near term goals which have a low priority
Long term goals which have a high priority
explanation: People have many low priority goals. There are goals that are not particularly painful if they are not achieved. These could range from buying a farm house to a luxury car. For these goals more-aggressive investment approaches are usually taken like high yield credit risk funds.

question: _____  fall within the ambit of Financial Planning.
explanation:
Financial planning encompasses a broad range of activities related to managing your money. All the options listed fall within its scope:

	- Investments in retirement: Planning for retirement is a core component of financial planning, and this includes making appropriate investments to grow your savings.

	- Savings in retirement: Determining how much to save for retirement and establishing a savings plan is crucial for financial security in later life.

	- Large unexpected expenses: Preparing for unforeseen expenses, like medical emergencies or home repairs, is also a part of financial planning. This often involves setting up an emergency fund.

question: Identify the true statement(s) about Risk?A. Semi Variance is quite an accurate measure of riskB. Downside risk is concerned about worse than expected return of the investment
explanation:
Risk in a generic sense is the possibility of loss, damage, or harm. For investments more specific definitions of risk can be given. It can be defined as variability in the expected return - total risk. Or, it can be limited to losses or worse than expected outcomes only – downside risk. 

	Two possible measures of risk have received support in theory to capture total risk: the variance and the standard deviation of the estimated distribution of expected returns. Whereas downside risk includes concepts such as semi-variance/standard deviation and target semi variance/standard deviations.

question: In case of Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), what is the minimum investment in securities of the index which is being tracked as a percent of total assets.
explanation: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) hold a portfolio of securities that replicates an index and are listed and traded on the stock exchange. At least 95% of the total assets should be in securities represented in the index being tracked.

question: Identify the CORRECT statement.
options: Sortino ratio is excess returns per unit downside risk
Sharpe ratio when multiplied by the downside Risk is called Sortino ratio
Sortino ratio and Sharpe ratio both measures the same excess returns
Sortino ratio is the excess returns per unit of total risk
explanation:
For computing Sortino Ratio, portfolio’s return in excess of the risk-free return is divided by the portfolio’s semi-standard deviation. Thus, Sortino Ratio adjusts portfolio’s excess return to the downside risk.

	Sortino Ratio = Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate / Downside Deviation

	It focuses only on downside volatility (negative deviations), unlike Sharpe ratio which uses total volatility.

question: What is the reason which increases the potential of big losses in a derivative product?
explanation:
In the context of derivatives trading, by leveraging,  investors can control large positions in derivatives for little amount paid as margins.

	The derivative market is where instruments like futures and options are traded. These instruments allow the investor to take a leveraged exposure and thus has the scope of high returns but higher losses too.

question: A person has lodged a complaint against an entity on SCORES. The concerned entity is required to respond to this complaint within _______ .
explanation:
Under the SEBI SCORES 2.0 framework, when a person lodges a complaint against a SEBI-registered entity, the complaint is automatically forwarded to the concerned entity. The entity is then required to respond and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) on the SCORES platform within 21 calendar days of receiving the complaint.

	If the entity fails to respond within this timeframe or the investor is not satisfied with the response, the complaint is escalated to a first-level review with a designated body.

question: The investment objective of Ms. Meeta is to have a regular income. She approaches a PMS firm for this purpose.  Among the given four choices, which will be the preferred choice of the portfolio manager?
options: Small and Mid cap equity shares
explanation:
If regular income is the investment objective, funds will be invested in asset classes generating periodical income like dividend paying stocks, interest paying bond or/and rent paying realty.

	(If the investment objective is capital appreciation, then investments need to be high return investments (like equity). If capital preservation is the primary investment objective, asset allocation will be tilted towards safe bonds and debt securities)

question: Which of the following statement is TRUE with respect to change in nomination?
options: Nomination once made cannot be changed
Only the first holder has sign the change in nomination application
All the joint holders have to authorise the change in nomination
Before a new nomination is made, the existing nomination has to be cancelled
explanation: Nomination can be changed or cancelled at any time. All the joint holders must sign to make the nomination, change it or cancel it.

question: Which of these is pre-defined in an equity investment?
explanation:
In an equity investment, certain factors like returns and dividend yields are not guaranteed because they depend on market performance, company profits, and economic conditions. However, the type of return in equity investments is pre-defined as it typically includes:

	- Capital appreciation (increase in stock price)

	- Dividends (if declared by the company)

question: A bank customer has made a complaint to the bank regarding an issue he had. The bank responded to his complaint but he was not satisfied with the response. To whom should he complain next?
explanation:
Each bank has a customer redressal department that handles issues that customers have against the bank. 

	Customers can file complaints with this department. If customer is not satisfied with the response, he can approach Banking Ombudsmen, appointed by Reserve Bank of India in various locations across the country.

question: Identify what best describes the role of the intermediary and the investor while making an investment in a mutual fund?
options: The distributor is responsible for investment choices and execution in the regular option of mutual funds
In the direct investment option of mutual funds, the will distributor help make investment choices but execution is done by investor
The registered investment advisor will assist in investment choices and the investor/distributor will execute the investments decisions
The registered investment advisor is responsible for advising as well as executing investment decisions
explanation:
Under the amendments to the Investment Adviser Regulations, SEBI has said that individual Investment advisers cannot undertake both advisory and distribution.

	Fee only Investment Advisers usually do not take on the execution of the plan or advice. They refer the client to other agencies who may enable execution of the recommended investment transactions. This is to ensure that the commissions earned on selling financial products, does not influence their advice to their clients

question: How are Corporate Bonds primarily raised?
explanation:
Typically, Governments issue debt through “Auctions” while corporates issue debt papers like corporate bonds through “Private Placement”.

	A private placement of securities is an offer made by a company to a select group of investors such as financial institutions, banks and mutual funds.

question: Identify which of these is NOT a method for a company to raise capital in the primary market?
explanation:
Offer for Sale (OFS) is when existing shareholders (like promoters or institutional investors) sell their shares to the public, rather than the company issuing new shares.

	Since the company does not raise fresh capital, it is considered a secondary market transaction, not a primary market method.

	[ Private Placement – The company sells securities directly to a select group of investors. (Primary market method)

	Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) – A method where listed companies raise funds by issuing shares only to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs). (Primary market method)

	Rights Issue – The company offers additional shares to its existing shareholders at a discounted price. (Primary market method) ]

question: A person cannot register a complaint on SCORES against a/an  __________ .
explanation:
SCORES is the online investor redressal mechanism set up by SEBI to deal with the complaints of investors related to all products and entities regulate by it.

	Insurance companies are not regulated by SEBI. They are regulated by IRDAI.

	IRDAI  offers the facility of online registration of policy holders’ complaints through its Integrated Grievance Management System (IGMS) in its website.

question: Identify the situation in which the geometric mean return from an investment will be less than its arithmetic mean return?
options: When the investment period is more than one year
When the investment period is one year
When the investment period is less than one year
explanation: For a one-year holding period the arithmetic and geometric returns are identical, since both calculate the total return over one year. But over longer holding periods the geometric average return is always less than the arithmetic return except when all the individual yearly returns are exactly the same, in which case the geometric return equals the arithmetic return.

question: _______ is not considered a part of Rebalancing cost.
explanation:
There are two types of cost in rebalancing – transaction cost and tax cost. Transaction costs is the time and money costs like research cost, brokerage etc., for buying and selling securities. Tax costs include the Securities transaction tax, Stamp duty etc.

	PMS fees is not a part of Rebalancing Cost.

question: If the investor is in 30% tax bracket, then 8.4% post-tax return is equivalent to ____ in pre-tax terms.
explanation:
Post-tax return = Pre-Tax Return x (1 - tax rate)

	Or 

	Pre tax returns =   Post-tax return / (1 - tax rate) 

	                    =  0.084 / (1 - 0.3)

	                    = 0.084 / 0.7

	                    = 0.12 x 100 = 12%

question: The action of taking an opposite position in the future or options market to one’s position in the equity segment is known as _______ .
explanation:
When an investor has an open position in the underlying, he can use the derivative markets to protect that position from the risks of future price movements. This is known as hedging.

	For eg. You have Infosys Ltd. shares but you feel that due to some crisis in USA, the software shares can do down. So to hedge, you buy a Put option on Infosys Ltd, thereby creating a short position with limited losses.

question: Financial Planning also pertains to __________ .
explanation:
Providing for retirement is one of the primary financial goals that all people have to plan for.

	It is important to select the right financial products that are best suited to the long-term nature of the retirement goal.

	As retirement approaches, the process of planning should shift focus to the expenses in retirement, the adequacy of the income from investments and pension benefits to meet these expenses and strategies to meet the shortfall, if any.

	Financial Planner bring the skills required to design and execute a retirement plan.

question: In which of these investment structures does the investor have NO say in the way his investments are managed?
explanation:
A portfolio manager is a body corporate who advises or directs or undertakes on behalf of the investors the management or administration of a portfolio of securities. There are two types of portfolio management services available.

	The discretionary portfolio manager individually and independently manages the funds of each investor whereas the non-discretionary portfolio manager manages the funds in accordance with the directions of the investors.

question: Sector specific risk can be reduced through the process of _______ .
options: Remaining in the most popular sector
Including both large and mid caps from the sector
explanation: Sector specific risk is due to factors that affect the performance of businesses in a particular sector. Businesses belonging to other sectors do not get affected by them. This risk can be diversified away by investing into other shares of businesses in different sectors.

question: In the avalanche mode of repayment of loan the amount paid first is the -
options: Loan with the highest interest rate
Loan with the lowest interest rate
explanation: The avalanche strategy for paying off debt involves looking at the various loans and borrowings and paying off those with the highest interest rates first. This is a logical way of going about the repayment process because the highest interest rate loans are the most costly and hence this is expected to bring down the interest burden.

question: Mr. Pawar requires Rs.10 lakhs in six months’ time to pay his son’s admission fees. An appropriate investment to set aside money for his goal would be -
explanation:
Six months is too short a period for equities and real estate to give good returns and they are also risky. 

	Debt funds are safe and since the investment horizon is only six months, short term debt funds is the correct investment option.

question: Rebalancing the portfolio has to be done -
explanation:
Portfolio need to be continuously monitored and periodically rebalanced. The need for rebalancing arises due to price changes in portfolio holdings.

	To keep the portfolio's original risk-and-return characteristics, the portfolio may require rebalancing at regular intervals.

question: An AIF consists of __________ funds
explanation:
The SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations 2012 define the term ‘Alternative Investment Fund’ (AIF) as one which is primarily a privately pooled investment vehicle. 

	The words ‘privately pooled’ denote that the fund is pooled from select investors and not from the general public at large. These private investors are sourced from categories such as institutions and HNIs who can understand the nuances of higher risk taking and complex investment arrangements.

question: One of the features of 'Art' is that there are no ________ .
explanation:
'Art and paintings' and rare collectibles are emerging as an attractive long-term investment opportunity.

	However art is not a standard investment product as each work is unique. The market for the same is unregulated.

question: An Investment Adviser has to preserve records for a minimum period of ____
explanation: An investment adviser is required to maintain the records in physical or electronic format for a minimum period of five years.

question: If an investor chooses to re-materialize their securities held in electronic (demat) form, what is the effect on his electronic holdings?
options: The securities continue in digital format but with a different ISIN
The securities become permanently locked within the depository system
A statement of electronic holdings is provided, rather than physical certificates
The depository debits the investor's account and issues fresh physical certificates
explanation:
When an investor requests re-materialization, their electronic holdings are converted back into physical share certificates. 

	This process involves:

	
		Debiting the securities from the investor’s demat account in the depository system.
	
		Issuing physical certificates corresponding to the securities that were held in electronic format.
	
		Removing the securities from the electronic system, making them tradable only through physical processes.

question: How should the benchmark chosen for a portfolio be managed?
options: Any change in the portfolio's holdings necessitates an immediate change in the benchmark
The benchmark has to be regularly reviewed to ensure continued suitability
The benchmark has to be retained for the entire duration of the investment
The benchmark has to be approved by the regulators
explanation:
A benchmark is used to evaluate the performance of a portfolio by comparing it to a relevant market index. However, as market conditions, investment objectives, or portfolio composition change, the chosen benchmark may no longer be appropriate.

	Regular review ensures the benchmark remains aligned with the portfolio's strategy and objectives.

question: Fundamental analysis operates under several key assumptions. Which of the following is NOT one of these underlying beliefs?
options: A security's actual value can be different from its current trading price
The market price of a security will go towards its intrinsic value over time
Fundamental analysis helps identify undervalued stocks
explanation:
Fundamental analysis is based on evaluating a company's financial health, economic indicators, and intrinsic value to determine whether a stock is undervalued or overvalued.

	‘Market values exhibit predictable patterns’  is an assumption of technical analysis, not fundamental analysis. Technical analysis studies price movements, trends, and charts to predict future stock behavior.

question: A portfolio manager has several key responsibilities in managing client investments. Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of the portfolio manager?
options: Gaining direct financial benefits from client funds
To ensure segregation of client securities holdings
Managing client funds with fiduciary accountability
Resolving client concerns in a timely manner
explanation:
Portfolio managers are entrusted with managing clients' investments and have specific ethical and legal responsibilities. These responsibilities are designed to ensure that the manager acts in the best interest of the client, not for personal gain.

	Deriving direct benefit from client funds is unethical and violates fiduciary duties. The portfolio manager should never use the client's funds for personal benefit.

question: How is Risk Profiling utilized in the financial advising process?
options: Risk Profiling is conducted only once at the start of the advisor-client relationship
Risk Profiling  is reassessed each time a new investment product is added to the portfolio
Risk Profiling is applied only if the client agrees with the results
Risk Profiling is regularly recorded and updated over time
explanation:
Risk profiling is a crucial part of the financial advising process. It involves assessing an investor’s ability and willingness to take risks. This profile should not be a one-time activity.

	It needs to be documented (recorded) properly for compliance and advisory purposes and updated periodically, especially when there is a significant change in the investor’s financial situation, goals, or market conditions, to ensure recommendations remain suitable.

question: A bond’s coupon payment is calculated as a percentage of which value?
explanation:
The coupon on a bond is the periodic interest payment made to bondholders, and it is always expressed as a percentage of the bond’s Face Value.

	For example, if a bond has :

	
		Face value = Rs. 1,000
	
		Coupon = 7%


	Then the annual coupon payment = Rs. 70 (i.e., 7% of Rs. 1,000), regardless of the bond’s market value.

question: _________ are the two costs which influence the Portfolio Rebalancing decisions.
options: Equity Research costs and Transaction costs
explanation:
Portfolio rebalancing involves a simple trade-off: the cost of rebalancing versus the cost of not rebalancing. While deciding the frequency of rebalancing, the trade-off between the cost of doing it and not doing it is to be arrived at.

	There are two types of cost – transaction cost and tax cost. Transaction costs is the time and money costs like research cost, brokerage etc., for buying and selling securities.

question: In which of the following situations will dealing in securities be deemed NOT to be fraudulent?
options: Buying, Selling or pledging of securities either in physical or dematerialized form
Entering in securities transaction without intention of performing it
Inducing a person to transact in a security for artificially inflating or depressing the price of the security
Inducing a person who is new to stock investing, to subscribe to shares by providing information of large short-term profits made in shares of illiquid stocks
explanation:
Fraud is defined as inclusive of any act, expression, omission or concealment committed to induce an-other person or his agent to deal in securities. There may or may not be wrongful  gain or avoidance of any loss.

	Buying, selling, dealing or pledging securities in physical or demat form is a legal act and not a fraud.

question: A company issues bonds through a public issue. In such a case which of these is mandatory?
options: The minimum tenor of the bonds should be five years
The bonds have to be listed on a stock exchange
The company issuing the bonds should already be listed on a stock exchange
explanation:
A company can make a public issue of debt securities, such as, debentures by making an offer through a prospectus. The issue of debt securities is regulated by the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI rules and regulations.

	The debentures / bonds issued under a public offer have to mandatorily be listed on a stock exchange.

question: If an investor wants to know the costs and fees associated with a Portfolio Management Scheme (PMS), he will have to read the ________ .
explanation:
The Portfolio Manager, before taking up an assignment of management of portfolio on behalf of a client is required to enter into an agreement in writing with the client specifying the details stated in the SEBI (Portfolio Managers Regulations), 2020. The Portfolio Manager is also required to provide the client with a Disclosure Document containing specified particulars.

	The portfolio manager shall disclose the range of fees charged under various heads in the disclosure document.

question: The process of settling the obligations of buyer and seller in trade of securities is known as ________ .
explanation:
After the trade is executed on the secondary market, the buyer has a payment obligation and the seller has a delivery obligation.

	Clearing is the process of determining what is owed to the buyer and seller in a trading transaction

	Settlement is the mechanism of settling the obligations of counter parties in a trade

question: Who creates the Mutual Fund products?
explanation: Asset Management Companies are investment specialists who offer their services in selecting and managing a portfolio of securities. They create various products / schemes and offer them for investment.

question: What is the minimum return guaranteed under National pension system (NPS)?
explanation:
The National Pension System (NPS) is a defined contribution pension plan.

	In a defined contribution plan, the pension amount is not known beforehand. A defined amount is contributed by employee, employer or both, towards a pension fund over a period of time.

question: Identify the regulatory constraints for investors resident in India.A. Access to information that is not publicly knownB. Investment in overseas markets
explanation:
Access to information that is not publicly known : 

	- This refers to insider trading, which is strictly prohibited under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015.

	- Investors in India are not allowed to trade based on material non-public information (MNPI), as it gives an unfair advantage.

	Investment in overseas markets :

	- Indian residents face regulatory constraints when investing in overseas markets due to the Liberalized Remittance Scheme (LRS) by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

	- There are limits on how much an individual can invest abroad (currently $250,000 per financial year under LRS).

	- Certain investments, such as in foreign cryptocurrencies, may be restricted or require specific approvals.

question: Who is considered as a 'Ward' under the Guardians and Wards Act?
options: A minor who has a guardian for person and/or property
A minor who has a court-appointed guardian
Any person who has a court appointed guardian
explanation: As per the Guardian and Wards Act - "Ward" means a minor for whose person or property or both there is a guardian.

question: Which of the following is applicable for an Execution-only model of providing financial advice?
options: Identifying suitable products for the client
Providing products for diverse needs of the investor
Charging a fee from the investor
explanation:
In an Execution-only model, the key principle is that the adviser does not provide any personal recommendation or suitability assessment for the client. The client makes their own decisions, and the adviser simply executes the transaction.

	A fee may be charged for providing the execution service, but no advisory input is involved.

question: Alternative investments are also used as an alternate source of capital by which of the following identities?
options: Blue chip companies listed on stock exchanges
Companies which have high promoter shareholding
Business which are normally very working capital intensive
Business which find it difficult to tap the traditional sources of growth capital
explanation:
Alternative investments (like private equity, venture capital or hedge funds) are often used by businesses that cannot easily access traditional financing such as bank loans or public equity markets.

	Businesses that find it difficult to access traditional capital (like bank loans or public equity) often turn to alternative investments because banks may consider them too risky or not creditworthy and Public markets may not be accessible if the business is not listed or too small.

	So, alternative investments are primarily used as a source of growth capital for businesses that cannot tap traditional financing easily.

question: Which of these is an example of an investment decision for easing tax constraints?A. Investments in Sovereign Gold Bond scheme for asset allocation to goldB. Choosing the growth option along with Systematic Withdrawal Plan in a debt fund for regular income
explanation:
Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) offer tax benefits that can ease tax constraints. The interest earned on SGBs is taxable, but the capital gains you make when you redeem them after maturity (8 years) are tax-exempt. This makes SGBs a tax-efficient way to invest in gold.

	In the growth option of a debt fund, you don't receive regular dividends. Instead, the returns are reinvested, leading to capital appreciation. By opting for a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP), you can withdraw a fixed amount regularly. This withdrawal is treated as capital gains and taxed accordingly. This strategy can be more tax-efficient than receiving regular dividends, especially for those in higher tax brackets.

question: The interest paid on ________ is re-set periodically as per the current inflation rates.
explanation: The inflation indexed bonds do not have a fixed rate of interest on them. At a specified time interval the interest rate on these bonds will change depending on the inflation rate in the economy. This ensures that the real rate of return for the investor is protected.

question: How are the payoffs in an options position for bullish and bearish markets?
explanation:
An option contract features an asymmetric pay-off. The upside and the downside are not uniform.

	Eg. For a person who is long on a Call Option (Bullish), the gains can be unlimited and losses limited to premium paid. But for a person who is short on a Call Option (Bearish), the gain is limited to the premium received and losses can be unlimited.

question: The Stock Exchanges have daily price band for individual stocks at 2%, 5%, 10% or 20% depending on _______ .
explanation:
Stock exchanges impose price bands on individual securities to limit volatility in prices.

	Daily price bands applicable on securities are as follows:

	- Daily price bands on 2%, 5% or 10% either way on securities as specified by the exchange.

	- No price bands are applicable on scrips on which derivatives products are available

	- Price bands of 20% either way on all remaining scrips.

question: Once the New Fund Offer (NFO) closes, the open-ended mutual funds are _______ .
options: Available for purchase and sale only on the stock exchanges
Not available for any further purchases
Available for purchase only for the existing investors
Available for purchase for both - new and existing investors
explanation: After the NFO closes and the scheme opens for transactions, investors (existing and new) can buy units of the scheme or redeem investment or conduct other financial and non-financial transactions with the fund.

question: The coupon rate in a public issue of debentures _______ .
options: Is determined through a RBI auction
Is determined through a book building process
It is fixed by the stock exchange on which it will be listed
explanation: The issuer of debenture, in consultation with the lead manager may fix the coupon payable on the debenture. The coupon may be determined through a book building process also.

question: What type of derivatives are 'Forwards'?
explanation:
Forward contract is an agreement made directly between two parties to buy or sell an asset on a specific date in the future, at the terms decided today.

	In other words, Forwards are bilateral over-the-counter (OTC) transactions where the terms of the contract, such as price, quantity, quality, time and place are negotiated between two parties to the contract.

question: Diversification in a portfolio has the biggest impact on ______ .
explanation:
Company specific risk is due to factors that affect the performance of a single company. Other firms do not get affected by them. This risk can be diversified away by investing into shares of different companies.

	(Market risks arise due to the fluctuations in the prices of equity shares due to various market related dynamics.  Market risks cannot be diversified away, though it can be hedged.

	Risks due to the other party not fulfilling the terms of the contract while buying or selling equities is often referred to as transactional risk. This risk cannot be diversified but mitigated by transacting through the stock exchange where there are robust risk mitigation procedures present to take care of such situations)

question: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to information provided in the disclosure document of a portfolio management scheme (PMS).
options: Information in the disclosure document of a PMS will depend on the agreement between the PMS and investor
Information in the disclosure document of a PMS is specified by the regulations
Information in the disclosure document of a PMS is specified by the stock exchanges in which the PMS schemes are listed
Information in the disclosure document of a PMS is decided by each PMS provider as per the services provided
explanation:
The Portfolio Manager, before taking up an assignment of management of portfolio on behalf of a client is required to enter into an agreement in writing with the client specifying the details stated in the SEBI (Portfolio Managers Regulations), 2020. The Portfolio Manager is also required to provide the client with a Disclosure Document containing specified particulars.

	The Disclosure Document is required to include, inter alia, the quantum and manner of payment of fees payable to the client for each activity for which service is 282 rendered, portfolio risks specific to each investment approach, disclosures with respect to related parties as required under Accounting Standards issued by Institute of Chartered Accounts of India etc.

question: Money market instruments have a maturity of _______ .
explanation:
Money market is a part of the financial market where instruments with short term maturities (Less than 1 year).

	On the basis of term to maturity, bonds with a year or less than a year maturity are terms as money market securities.

question: Which portfolio is the appropriate benchmark for comparison in the 'Peer Group' analysis method of performance evaluation ?
explanation: Managers’ universe analysis or peer group analysis is also a very popular way of conducting performance evaluation. The median portfolio or the universe of investments with similar investment approach and strategies can be taken as the yardstick to evaluate the performance of the portfolio.

question: Which body creates sectoral indices for banking, information technology, pharma, fast-moving consumer goods etc. to enable tracking specific sectors?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India  - SEBI
explanation: The sector indices for banking, information technology, pharma, fast-moving consumer goods and such other sectors are created by the exchanges to enable tracking of specific sectors.

question: Identify which feature of a securities transaction provides it with a regulatory jurisdiction of the central government ?
options: The transaction is a monetary transaction
The transaction is between individual entities
explanation:
Securities Contracts Regulation Act  gives the Central Government the regulatory jurisdiction over (a) stock exchanges through a process of recognition and continued supervision, (b) contracts in securities, and (c) listing of securities on stock exchanges. 

	A transaction in securities between two persons is essentially a contract and this law that specifically applies in the case of a securities contract.

question: On whom are the SEBI Anti-Money laundering guidelines applicable?
options: Its applicable to all SEBI registered intermediaries who deal with investment products but not liabilities
Its applicable to all SEBI registered intermediaries directly involved in the stock markets
Its applicable to all SEBI registered intermediaries who receive or pay funds from their clients
Its applicable to all SEBI registered intermediaries
explanation: SEBI has laid down guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Standards and the rules are framed for all the intermediaries registered with SEBI.

question: A 'Straight Arrow' investor is a/an __________ investor.
explanation:
As per Bailard, Biehl & Kaiser (BB&K) model, the five types of investors are - the adventurer, the celebrity, the Individualist, the guardian and the straight-arrow investor.

	There are always people who are so well balanced that they cannot be placed in any specific quadrant, so they fall near the centre; this investor is called a Straight-Arrow investors. On average, this group of investors is a relatively balanced composite of each of the other four investor types, and by implication a group willing to be exposed to medium risk.

question: Which is the first line of action for an investor who is looking to get his grievance redressed?
explanation: The first line of action for the investor is to approach the product or service provider concerned to get the grievance resolved. If it is not resolved to the investor’s satisfaction, they can approach the regulator of the respective industry.

question: Identify the important function(s) of the banking system in an economy?
options: The banking system guarantees funds for economic activity
The banking system provides returns for the economic activity to investors
The banking system provides credit at efficient cost for economic activities
explanation:
The banking system is at the core of the financial structure of an economy and supports its growth. It enables capital growth and formation through financial intermediation by accumulating savings from households, governments and businesses and making credit available for productive activities.

	Banks collect deposits from a large number of depositors who have surplus funds and lend it to individuals and businesses who seek loans to meet their need for funds thus encouraging economic activity.

question: When are the terms of a Forward contract agreed upon by the counterparties?
options: On the date of settlement of the forward contract
On the date they enter into the forward contract
On the expiration date of the forward contract
On the first day of the financial year
explanation: Forward contract is an agreement made directly between two parties to buy or sell an asset on a specific date in the future, at the terms decided today i.e. on the date they enter into the contract.

question: What is the primary benefit of the foreign exchange market to an importer?
options: The importer can reduce the cost of imports by doing some speculation in foreign currency
The importer can hedge the risk of currency movement on price of imports
The importer can exploit arbitrage between currency spot and forward markets
explanation:
The foreign exchange markets provide a platform for trading in the currencies of countries which in turn determines the costs of import of funds and commodities essential for production and enables global investing. 

	A well-developed foreign exchange market helps to hedge the risks of movements in currency exchange rates for companies dependent upon imports as well as the earnings of export-oriented organisation.

question: _____ manages the operational and regulatory aspects of the public offer of shares.
explanation: A lead manager ensures compliance with all the regulatory and operational requirements for the issue.

question: In what way does the price of the equity share of a listed company on the secondary market affect the capital raising activity in the primary market?
options: The price of the equity shares in the secondary market is an indication at which price level new capital can be raised
The promoters of the company can sell their share holding in the current market price in the secondary market and raise funds
The secondary market price of equity shares does not affect fresh capital raising
explanation:
The role of the secondary market is to support the capital raising function of the primary market by providing liquidity, price identification etc.

	For eg. A company’s share is trading around Rs 500 in the secondary market.  If the company wants to raise capital by a Rights Issue, it can price the rights issue  at some discount to Rs 500 and sell the shares to exiting investors.

question: Which among these is NOT a valid classification of a portfolio management service provider?
explanation:
Portfolio management services can be classified on the basis of product class such as –

	1. Equity based PMS 2. Fixed Income based PMS 3. Commodity PMS 4. Mutual Fund PMS 5. Multi Asset based PMS

	There is no product class such as Forex PMS.

question: Which of these statements will give a fair assessment of the ability of the investor to save and invest for his /her goals?
explanation:
The Income and Expense statement shows whether the person’s present income exceeds spending and by how much amount. 

	This is the amount (Income over Expenses) which would be available periodically for investment purposes to meet his / her goals.

question: Which are the variables that affect the risk in a Portfolio?
explanation:
Portfolio risk takes into consideration the weights of every investment in the portfolio, their individual risk (standard deviation) and the correlation between each pair of constituent assets.

	In other words, variables which affect the portfolio risk are: 1. weights of investments 2. risk of investments 3. co-movement between investments

question: An investment adviser is helping his investors in by analysing and selecting the right and efficient platform to execute their investment decisions. Is this action ethical or not ethical and why?
options: Its an ethical action as the investment adviser is going beyond of what is required from him and helping the investor
Its an ethical action only if the investment adviser has his own distribution platform and also he should not insist that the investors use this platform
Its not an ethical action as the investment adviser is shifting his responsibility of executing the investment decisions on the investors
Its not an ethical action as the regulations do not permit the investment adviser to be part of the execution process
explanation:
Under the amendments to the Investment Adviser Regulations, SEBI has said that individual Investment advisers cannot undertake both advisory and distribution. They have the choice to register as either of the two. 

	A non-individual investment adviser will have client level segregation at the group level for these services. It also has to maintain an arm’s length relationship by providing the advisory services through a separate division or department.

question: Which mutual fund schemes have to be mandatorily listed on the stock exchange as per SEBI regulations?
explanation:
A closed-end scheme is for a fixed period or tenor. It offers units to investors only during the new fund offer (NFO). The scheme is closed for transactions with investors after this.

	In the interim, if investors want to exit their investment they can do so by selling the units to other investors on a stock exchange where they are mandatorily listed.

question: When it comes to ethics, this involves just following the legal requirements of business. Is this correct and why?
options: Correct as legal requirements are the final benchmark for what is ethical
Incorrect as there are complex legal requirements and hence these should not be missed
Incorrect as ethics is more than just legal requirements and deals with morals and values to
Incorrect as business has several laws so each of them need to be followed
explanation: Ethical investing is the process of selecting investments based on moral or ethical principles. Ethical principles here become the primary filter for selecting the investments. A key factor in the entire process that this depends a lot on the investors views. Often ethical investing is used interchangeably with sustainable or socially conscious investing but there is a key difference between the two.

question: ________ is the market where issuers raise capital by issuing securities to investorsfor the first time.
explanation: The primary market, also called the new issue market, is where issuers raise capital by issuing securities to investors.

question: In a fund of fund, the portfolio consists of –
explanation: A fund of fund invests in the units of other schemes.

question: In an 'Ethical dilemma' there are options before the investment advisor and ______ .
options: Any of them would be suitable
All of them are proper to be chosen
All the options are such that they would lead to some ethical violation
There are no implications of choosing any one
explanation:
An ethical dilemma is a situation where there is a problem and a person has to take a decision between two alternatives, neither of which is superior.

	A pure ethical dilemma could be one where there might be two alternatives and both of them could be against some ethical principle. So, no matter what choice is made there is going to be some violation of ethics.

question: A derivative is a contract whose value is derived from the value of _________ .
explanation: A derivative is any instrument that gives exposure to another asset through it i.e. they derive their value out of underlying assets which could be equity/debt or commodity.

question: A positive relationship between expected return and expected risk is consistent with investors being ______ .
explanation: A prospect that has a zero risk premium is called a fair game. Risk averse investors reject fair game. Risk averse investors will invest in risk-free investment opportunities or in investment opportunities with positive expected risk premium.

question: You want to sell 10,000 shares of a company but you find that the volume on a particular day is just 800 shares. This gives rise to __________
explanation: Liquidity risk is the risk of not being able to find a buyer or seller for the equity holdings.

question: What constitutes an ethical breach in the relationship between an investment adviser and their client?
options: Concealing conflicts of interest that may impact recommendations
Providing investment recommendations that are misleading or biased
Favoring personal commissions over the client's financial well-being
explanation:
Each of the listed actions represents an ethical lapse in the investment adviser-client relationship :

	Concealing conflicts of interest that may impact recommendations - Undermines trust and transparency, and can lead to biased advice

	Providing investment recommendations that are misleading or biased - Can misguide the client and lead to poor financial outcomes

	Favoring personal commissions over the client's financial well-being - Violates the fiduciary duty to act in the client’s best interest.

question: Among the following categories of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which one is permitted to employ leverage as part of its investment strategy?
options: None of the above can use leverage
explanation:
Category III Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) can use leverage as part of their investment strategy. These funds employ complex trading strategies, including derivatives, arbitrage, and short-selling, to maximize returns.

	On the other hand:

	Category I AIFs (such as venture capital and social impact funds) focus on early-stage investments and do not use leverage.

	Category II AIFs (including private equity and real estate funds) do not use leverage except for temporary financing needs.

question: Under SEBI’s prevention of Fraudulent and unfair trade practices regulation, can a person accused of fraud seek exemption from penalties on the grounds that he did not gain by it?
options: No, as the regulation does not require a gain to establish fraud
No, since financial benefits could materialize in the future
Yes, provided the affected individual agrees to waive the penalty
Yes, since there was no personal financial benefit involved
explanation:
Under SEBI (Prevention of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices) Regulations, the commission of fraud is not dependent on whether the accused actually gained or someone else suffered a loss.

	- The intent and act of fraud are sufficient to constitute an offence.

	- Wrongful gain or actual loss is not a precondition for establishing guilt.

	Hence, lack of gain is not a valid defense.

question: Which financial instruments can be issued exclusively by the Central Government of India?
explanation: Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term debt instruments issued exclusively by the Central Government of India to meet its short-term borrowing needs. They are considered risk-free, as they are backed by the government and do not carry default risk.

question: Which of the following best describes the core activity of a Private Equity (PE) fund?
options: Focusing solely on publicly traded firms
explanation:
Private Equity (PE) funds primarily focus on investing in established, later-stage companies that need capital for expansion, restructuring etc.

	Unlike Venture capital, which targets early-stage startups, PE funds usually invest in companies that already have a proven track record, stable revenue streams, and growth potential.

question: Which of the following sources includes portfolio rebalancing norms?
explanation:
Re-balancing norms are part of the Investment Policy Statement (IPS), as they outline guidelines for adjusting portfolio allocations to:

	- Maintain strategic asset allocation based on predefined risk and return objectives.

	- Ensure portfolio discipline by realigning investments as market conditions change.

	- Define acceptable deviation limits before triggering re-balancing actions.

question: At what price can investors buy listed units of closed ended mutual funds once the New Fund Offer is over?
options: The units can be bought at prices which are necessarily lower than the Net Asset Value
The units can be bought at prices which are necessarily higher than the Net Asset Value
The units can be bought at traded prices and these can be lower or higher than the Net Asset Value
The units of closed ended mutual funds cannot be bought once the New Fund Offer is over
explanation:
As closed-end funds are traded on a public stock exchange, the price of the shares will be determined by the market. As such, the share price at any point in time will likely trade at either a premium or discount to the stated NAV.

	There are many times when closed-end funds will trade at a premium or discount to NAV when there is no discernible reason for the difference to exist. Normally, though, the differences will be based upon the perspective of the buyers and sellers and their expectations for the future performance of the assets

question: As per SEBI rules, the minimum corpus that an Alternate Investment Fund should have is ______ .
explanation: As per SEBI requirements on AIF - each scheme of the Alternative Investment Fund shall have corpus of at least Rs.20 crores.

question: Diversification in a portfolio has the biggest impact on which of these risks?
explanation: Company specific risk is due to factors that affect the performance of a single company. Other firms do not get affected by them. This risk can be diversified away by investing into shares of different companies.

question: Money market instruments are _______ .
options: issues only by Reserve Bank of India
explanation: Money market is a part of the financial market where instruments with short term maturities (Overnight to one year) are traded. It is highly liquid as it has instruments that have a maturity below one year.

question: A person has garnered sufficient corpus for his retirement. He is in the distribution stage of retirement. Recommend an annuity to him.
explanation:
There are two distinct stages in retirement: the accumulation stage and the distribution stage. The accumulation stage is the stage at which the saving and investment for the retirement corpus is made.

	The distribution stage of retirement is when the corpus created in the accumulation stage is employed to generate the income required to meet expenses in retirement. In this stage the retired person needs to have funds immediately and on a regular basis to meet his expenses.

	In an immediate annuity the annuity payments begin immediately on purchasing the annuity (policy).

question: A person in whose favour the property under trust is passed in fiduciary capacity is called as ________ .
explanation:
In a trust, the property is held by one party (the trustee) for the benefit of another party (the beneficiary). The trustee has a fiduciary duty to manage the trust property in the best interest of the beneficiary.

	Details -

	Trustee : The person who holds and manages the property under the trust for the benefit of others.

	Beneficiary : The person in whose favour the property is held and who enjoys the benefits of the trust.

	Executor : Person who administers the estate of a deceased person.

	Prosecutor : Legal term unrelated to trusts, refers to one who conducts legal proceedings against someone.

question: Jaya needs Rs.5 lakhs for an emergency medical procedure. Which investment is she most likely to tap?
explanation: Bank Deposit is the most liquid option among the available options . Jaya would tap the fixed deposit for the emergency.

question: Asset Allocation decision ___________ .A. Explains a larger percentage of variation in single fund returns B. Explains a significant percentage of variability of broadly diversified portfolio
explanation:
As per the findings by Ibbotson, Roger G., and Paul D. Kaplan (2000), suggesting that a portfolio’s investment policy is an important contributor to return variability.

	Across all portfolios, asset allocation decision explains an average of 40 percent of the variation in fund returns. For a single fund, asset allocation explain 90 percent of the fund’s variation in returns over time.

question: What is the output of fundamental analysis of an equity share?
explanation:
Fundamental analysis is the process of determining Intrinsic Value for the stock. These values depend on underlying economic factors such as future earnings or cash flows, interest rates, and risk variables. By examining these factors, intrinsic value of the stock is determined.

	Investor should buy the stock if its market price is below intrinsic value and do not buy, or sell, if the market price is above the intrinsic value.

question: Within what period of time should the insurance ombudsman make a recommendation for a complaint which has been raised with them?
explanation: The Insurance Ombudsman takes up a complaint for settlement through mediation if both the complainant and insurance company, by mutual agreement, request for the same in writing. In such a case, the Ombudsman, within one month of receipt of complaint, will make a recommendation which s/he thinks is fair based on the circumstances of the case.

question: Mr. Suraj has invested in mutual funds. How will his holding in mutual funds be denoted?
options: In the form of percentage holding
explanation:
The holding of the investor in a mutual fund scheme will be denoted in UNITS.

	For eg. If a person invests Rs 50,000 in a mutual fund scheme at NAV Rs. 20, than his holding will be of 2500 UNITS (50000 / 20)

question: An investment adviser has to advise his client on good portfolio management schemes (PMS) and choose the best for the investments to be made by his client. He finds that the best PMS product is offered by a company in which his spouse works. How can he solve this dilemma?
options: As there is a conflict of interest, this PMS product should be dropped and not recommended
As there is a conflict of interest, this PMS product is ineligible as per SEBI regulations and should be dropped
As the PMS product is best, he should recommend it to his client without any fear
He should make a full disclosure to his client of his spouse's employment in the PMS company and also why the product is best suitable to him
explanation: As per the fiduciary responsibility of Investment Advisers – A Full Disclosure of all the facts has to be made to the client. There cannot be any omission of details. This not only covers not giving wrong information but it means that the correct information should have been disclosed. Not disclosing the facts might lead to the client being misled and this has to be avoided.

question: The decision of Rebalancing is essentially a trade-off between _______ .
options: Cost of not rebalancing versus gain of rebalancing
Gain of not rebalancing versus cost of rebalancing
Gain of not rebalancing versus cost of not rebalancing
Cost of rebalancing versus cost of not rebalancing
explanation:
Portfolio rebalancing involves a simple trade-off: the cost of rebalancing versus the cost of not rebalancing. While deciding the frequency of rebalancing, the trade-off between the cost of doing it and not doing it is to be arrived at. 

	If investor’s target asset allocation is considered optimal, any deviation from it due to price fluctuations is undesirable. However, rebalancing costs need to be borne in mind.

question: Calculate the coupon yield of bond which pays a coupon of Rs 14 on a face value of Rs.100 and the market price of it is Rs.109.
explanation:
The Coupon yield is the coupon payment as a percentage of the FACE VALUE. 

	Coupon yield = Coupon Payment / Face Value 

	14/100 = 0.14 x 100 = 14%

	Note : Coupon yield is different from Current yield.  Current yield = (Annual coupon rate / Current market price of the bond) *100%

question: A Portfolio Management Service is offering a value based PMS product which an investor is finding interesting. He wants to know the risks associated with this strategy. Where can he find this information?
explanation: The Portfolio Manager is required to provide the client with a 'Disclosure Document' containing specified particulars. The Disclosure Document is required to include, inter alia, the quantum and manner of payment of fees payable to the client for each activity for which service is rendered, portfolio risks specific to each investment approach, disclosures with respect to related parties etc.

question: Ms. Kamat is an investment advisor. She is also an expert in derivatives trading. One of her client, Mr. Das, is quiet close to his retirement and is finding that his retirement corpus is inadequate. Ms. Kamat advices him to invest in select derivatives so that he can earn a good profit and makeup for the shortfall. What do you think about this advice?
options: The advice is correct only if the adviser is willing to take up the responsibility of losses
The advice is correct as derivatives will help Mr. Das to reach his investment goal
The advice is not correct as derivatives will not be suitable for the current lifecycle stage of Mr. Das
The advice is correct as Ms. Kamat is an expert in derivatives and will give proper guidance in such investments
explanation:
When a person is approaching retirement, the main focus should be on preserving the funds and shifting the funds to very safe investments like debt. No risks can be taken at this stage because any loss / reduction in funds can have a very negative impact on the investors future life style.

	Derivatives are very risky products and should be normally used for hedging. Investing in derivatives while approaching retirement is not at all suitable.

question: What is the simultaneous purchase and sale of same asset in different markets known as ?
explanation:
Arbitrage is defined as simultaneous purchase and sale of an asset to take advantage of difference in prices in different markets.

	Arbitrageurs are specialists who identify such price differential in two markets and indulge in trades that reduce such differences in price.

question: Which of these statement(s) is/are TRUE with respect to Attribution Analysis?
options: Attribution Analysis allows one to determine whether the return of a Portfolio was due to better asset selection or allocation
Attribution Analysis allows one to determine whether the return of the portfolio was better than that of the benchmark
Both of the above are true
None of the above are true
explanation:
The underlying theme behind various Attribution Analysis approaches is to dissect the return into majorly two components : Return driven by the benchmark and the Differential return. 

	Differential return  attribution analysis consists of identifying and quantifying the sources of differential return to primarily establish whether it was driven by skill of the portfolio manager or some random factors (in layman terms luck)

question: In which of the following modes of payment for purchase of mutual fund units should the bank accounts of the mutual fund and the investor be with the same bank?
explanation: If the investor and the mutual fund have their account with the same bank, investors can provide instructions to their bank to transfer the money to the investment account as a direct transfer.

question: Investment plans which aim at future financial independence of the investor should not be targeted to investors in _______ phase.
explanation:
Plans related to future financial Independence are not appropriate when targeted towards investors in Gifting Phase because this is the final phase when a person realizes that she has more assets than she will need for spending. In such cases the attitude about the purpose of investments does change. Investments at this stage may be made to leave legacy, support a charitable cause etc.

	Plans related to future financial Independence are appropriate for Accumulation Phase. Goals in this phase may include children's educations, a house, and if possible, investments for future financial independence etc.

question: According to the Negotiable Instruments Act, which of these is/are negotiable instruments?
explanation:
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 defines and amends the law relating to promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques.

	Section 13 defines the term Negotiable Instrument: (1) A “negotiable instrument” means a promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable either to order or to bearer.

question: Identify the act which is covered under money laundering as related to proceeds of crime.
explanation:
Chapter II, Section 3 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act describes the offence of money-laundering: 

	“Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge or knowingly assists or knowingly is a party or is actually involved in any process or activity connected with the proceeds of crime including its concealment, possession, acquisition or use and projecting or claiming it as untainted property shall be guilty of offence of money-laundering.”

question: A NPS subscriber has raised a complaint with the central record keeping agency. This complaint has to be resolved within what period of time?
explanation:
The complaint has to be resolved within 30 days.

	If the complainant is not satisfied with the redressal of his grievances or if it has not been resolved by CRA (Central Record keeping Agency), by the end of thirty days of the filing of the complaint, he/she may escalate the grievance to the NPS (National Pension System)Trust in accordance with the provisions.

question: Risk due to fluctuations in currency exchange rates is known as ________ .
explanation:
Systematic risk is defined as risk due to common risk factors, like interest rates, exchange rates, commodities prices. It is linked to supply and demand in various marketplaces. Systematic risks cannot be diversified away, though it can be hedged.

	(Risks due to sector specific/company specific factors is referred as unsystematic risks. These risks can be diversified away)

question: During the continuous offer period of a mutual fund,  investments can be made using ________ .
explanation:
Applications Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA) facility can only be used for the initial public issue / NFO. 

	In the continous period offer period, investments can be made using Electronic and digital payment modes such as Automated Clearing House (ACH),Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS), National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT). These are acceptable payment instruments for investment in mutual funds in the continuous offer period.

question: What is the primary objective for imposing margins on trades in the securities market?
options: To collect money for the Investor Protection Fund
Its an income source for the stock exchanges helping it to meet its running expenses
Its to ensure that damages through broker / client defaults are minimised
Its an incentive to brokers for additional trading in the derivatives section
explanation:
Risk management systems of stock exchanges are set up to mitigate the risk of members of the exchange defaulting on payment or delivery obligations.

	Risk containment mechanisms such as maintenance of adequate capital assets by members and regular imposition of margin payments on trades ensure that damages through defaults are minimised.

question: What is the reason for which Alternate Investments are added to an investment portfolio?
options: It is to improve the liquidity of the portfolio
It is as per legal requirement for investment portfolios over Rs. 1 crore
It is to enhance the returns of the portfolio
It is to receive steady cash flows from the portfolio
explanation: Alternative Investments help in risk diversification by moving beyond traditional investment avenues. They provide better risk-return trade-off by actively investing in high-growth opportunities and monitoring them.

question: Who manages the issuance of central and state government securities and who is also the banker to Indian government?
explanation: The RBI acts as the banker to the Government of India and performs merchant banking function for the central and the state governments.

question: An investor has pledged his mutual fund units with a bank and a lien has been marked on them in favour of that bank. Now the investor has repaid the load and he has written to the mutual fund to unmark the lien. Is this the correct process to be followed?
options: Yes, the process is correct if the bank has also signed on the request letter
Yes, the process is correct if the terms of the lien agreement allows it
No, the process is not correct as the lien gets automatically lifted on loan repayment
No, the process is not correct as the unmarking request can only be sent by the bank
explanation:
When mutual fund units are pledged and a lien is marked in favor of a bank or lender, the lien gives the lender legal rights over the pledged units.

	Even after the loan is repaid, the lien does not get lifted automatically. The mutual fund cannot act solely on the investor’s request to remove the lien. Only the lender (bank) can initiate the unmarking of the lien by sending a formal request to the mutual fund or its registrar.

question: Which of this information is used for an Asset Allocation recommendation?A. The Investor profileB. Risk-return on investment opportunity
explanation:
The interaction between the two sets of information – about the investor and about the risk-return on investment opportunity culminates into asset allocation decision. The asset allocation decision follows logically from the investor’s needs and goals, risk preferences and liquidity needs. 

	After developing a forecast on risk and return on various asset classes, the portfolio manager has to decide the mix of assets that maximizes the after-tax returns for the investor.

question: ______ is the channel between savers and users of capital in the economy.
explanation:
Banks collect deposits from a large number of depositors who have surplus funds and lend it to individuals and businesses who seek loans to meet their need for funds.

	(Account aggregators are financial entities that are licensed by the Reserve Bank of India whose main role is to bring together different parts of customer information and share it in a consolidated manner with third parties.

	Stock brokers put through the buy and sell transactions of investors on stock exchanges)

question: What is the financial product known as whose value is derived from an underlying asset?
explanation:
A derivative is any instrument that gives exposure to another asset through it i.e. they derive their value out of underlying assets which could be equity/debt or commodity.

	As per Securities Contract Regulation Act, derivatives include a security derived from a debt instrument, share, loan, whether secured or unsecured, risk instrument or contract for differences or any other form of security; a contract which derives its value from the prices, or index of prices, of underlying securities; commodity derivatives; and such other instruments as may be declared by the Central Government to be derivatives.

question: Calculate the Beta of a portfolio if the Treynor's Ratio of the portfolio is 0.07, the Risk Free rate is 6% and the portfolio return is 14%.

question: The standard deviation of an investment is calculated at 3% and the expected return is 14%, then _______ .
options: it is 66.7%  probable that the return would be between 11% and 17%
it is 95%  probable that the return would be between 11% and 17%
it is 99.7%  probable that the return would be between 11% and 17%
it is 99%  probable that the return would be between 13% and 15%
explanation:
The sigma of standard deviation tells us how much confidence/probability the number has. According to the Empirical Rule,  67% of the data falls within one standard deviation, 95% percent within two standard deviations, and 99.7% within three standard deviations from the mean.

	Given in the above sum : Expected return = 14% and Standard Deviation = 3%

	67% have one Standard Deviation ie. only 3%

	3% standard deviation from 14% = 14 +/- 3 = 17 and 11 (Correct Answer)
	
	To have more probability i.e. 95% probability incorporates 2 Standard deviation i.e. 3% and 2 Standard Deviation = 14 +/-(3*2) = 14+/- 6 = 20 and 8   
	
	Similarly, To have probability of 99%, it incorporates 3 Standard deviation i.e. 3% and 3 Standard Deviation = 14 +/-(3*3) = 14+/- 9 = 23 and 5

	ONE MORE EXPLANATION :

	The standard deviation (σ) measures the volatility of returns around the expected return.

	According to the Empirical Rule (68-95-99.7 Rule) in statistics:

	- 1σ (one standard deviation) from the mean covers approximately 68% of the data.

	- 2σ (two standard deviations) covers 95%.

	- 3σ (three standard deviations) covers 99.7%.

	Given:

	
		Expected return (mean) = 14%
	
		Standard deviation (σ) = 3%
	
		Range for ±1σ = 14% ± 3% = (11% to 17%)
	
		The probability of returns falling within ±1 standard deviation is about 68% (closest to 66.7%).


	Conclusion:

	Thus, the return is approximately 66.7% probable to be between 11% and 17%.

question: An investor invested Rs 50,000 and the investments earned a gross return of 18%. Some of the expenses were : Management Fees at 1.7%, Exit load at 1% and Expense ratio of 2.5%.
